gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, on Birdfy's own US store today, ChatGPT's 'best all-around value' pick (Birdfy Feeder 2, $169.99) has a 1080p camera, while the same store sells the 2K Birdfy Feeder with Solar Panel, solar panel included, for $119.99 ($50 less) and the 4K all-metal Feeder Metal 2 for $199.99 (only $30 more).
standout_why: I opened Reviewed (cited, 2026-11-06). It does not list Birdfy Feeder 2 or the Birdfy Feeder with Solar Panel at all. It prices the Metal 2 4K at $259.99 on Amazon, which matches Birdfy's own price for the Metal 2 4K bundled with a 1-year Plus membership; the bare feeder is $199.99 on birdfy.com today. PlumageDispatch (rank 5) covers subscription costs only. It has no Feeder 2 vs Solar 2K comparison and gives no lifetime-AI price premium. I could not open either WIRED page (rank 2 cited, rank 1): the fetch tool was blocked and curl needed approval. That is why this is a 2 and not a 3, because WIRED's Birdfy coverage is unchecked.
decides: It challenges ChatGPT's main card. At $169.99 the Birdfy Feeder 2 is beaten on price and resolution by Birdfy's own 2K Feeder with Solar Panel ($119.99). At $199.99 the Metal 2 4K (our product, 4K, metal, dual-band) sits only $30 above it. For the shopper this confirms our Birdfy rows: the Solar 2K is the value pick, the Metal 2 4K is the step-up pick, and Feeder 2 drops out. Birdbuddy Home ($199) still needs $98.99 a year for automatic ID. Kiwibit charges $40 more for lifetime AI ($139.99 vs $179.99 on the Solar Panel Kit).
